title: The World of Kira
summary: A homebrew fantasy world spanning the mapped regions of Larius, TalmahKah, Aldain, Azaloth, Falkion and Bendara. Its surviving written histories centre on Larius in 1342 A.A., where dwarven industry, elven republics and human kingdoms live with the aftermath of their wars.

binding.role: World-specific reference content using existing Core and genre systems.

readiness.reason: World guide available. Dated starting snapshots and setting rules are in development.

canon_policy.source_material: Original user-supplied documents preserved byte for byte.
canon_policy.record_summaries: Editorial organization of legacy claims, not newly enacted world events.
canon_policy.conflicts: Unresolved claims retain their source and are listed separately; no new explanation is made canon.
canon_policy.knowledge: Out-of-character setting reference; not automatically received character knowledge.
canon_policy.continuing_worlds: References never reset or overwrite committed playthrough state.
canon_policy.future_events: Legacy plot threads are not scheduled outcomes.

guide.title: The World of Kira
guide.subtitle: Larius and the lands beyond · world reference v0.1

sections.title: Larius in 1342 A.A.
paragraphs: The dwarves of Akaria rose into a world already inhabited by elves and humans. Their Ascension began a new calendar. More than a thousand years later, the nations of Larius live with the borders, grievances and alliances left by their wars.

The surviving histories name 1342 A.A. as present day. Akaria holds its underground empire and surface cities. Sadion is ruled by Erik Vollan. Everwood remains an elven republic, while Kyrinus has its own council and a renewed relationship with its former homeland. Estru’s southern lands trade with the dwarves.

sections.title: The nations of Larius
paragraphs: Akaria began beneath Iron Hill, where Barvaris Akarian brought the dwarven clans under one banner. Karkaria became the heart of its roads and cities. Emperor Cathius Akarian now favours trade and further underground expansion. Dwarven factories, firearms and gunpowder give the empire a distinctive place among its neighbours.

Sadion grew from the settlements of the Sadire into a kingdom centred on Bay Watch. Grad Vollan founded the Legion of Valiance, and San Vollan established a navy and Hunter corps. The kingdom’s history remembers both its alliance with Everwood and its crushing victory over Estru.

Everwood’s elves survived disease, civil war and the fall of their monarchy. The Grand Republic of Evalia governs through representatives of its cities and villages. Its old colony Kyrinus became independent after rebellion, but the two elven nations now share trade and a non-aggression pact.

Estru also broke from its former homeland. Its later attack on Sadion ended in defeat. Southern Estru appears in the surviving records as a trading partner of Akaria and a client of the Rangers of Larius. The exact present divisions of Estru still need to be recovered.

sections.title: Peoples and distant lands
paragraphs: The Larius list names dwarves, Sadire humans, Estrusians and six Evalian elven groups: Flatland, Ice, Mountain, Forest, Sea and Desert. The histories distinguish Evalian and Karthinian political communities; nationality and elven ancestry are not interchangeable.

The TalmahKah map names thirty-two locations, including temples, watches, settlements and five communities grouped under Lupine Tribes: Woshi, Foxti, Nekhamen, Coyota and Dingishi. The Word list gives Lupine height and weight ranges; their societies and relations still need fuller accounts.

sections.title: The original maps
paragraphs: Larius survives as a numbered Minecraft reference map. Its key distinguishes cities, underground cities, capitals and castles. Bay Watch, Griffin, Forlathis, Tethris, Estru City, Castle LuCain, Vlaris and Cthulis connect the map with the written accounts.

TalmahKah has a separate numbered map. Its place names extend from BogTown and IceCrown through Prenceta Temple, Scrap Haven and Turtle Rock to the named Lupine communities. These are places to develop from the source, not evidence that their cultures or political relationships are already known.

Both maps are retained as original references with no established campaign date or distance scale. Some labels differ from the histories, and the Larius key repeats number 25. The gazetteers preserve those differences.

sections.title: Aldain and the other mapped regions
paragraphs: Aldain’s map has an explicit political colour key. Light blue represents the Scalian Scalix Imperium; red the Rolling Hills Tribe; yellow the Mountain Peak Tribe; green the Eversong Hollow Tribe; blue the Frozen Lake Tribe; and purple the Primatarus Shenyan Republic.

Its eleven numbered entries name Hissinberg, Salazar, Rotten Stump, the four tribes, Shindu Temple, Shenyang, Chirac and Chengdu. The states’ names and mapped associations are supplied; their rulers, peoples, histories and relationships still await fuller accounts.

Azaloth and Bendara are represented by terrain maps without supplied place keys or political labels. Falkion’s map shows a small main landmass surrounded by water. The cyan line around it has no supplied explanation. These three maps establish named regions to develop without inventing their inhabitants or governments.

Larius, TalmahKah, Aldain, Azaloth, Falkion and Bendara sit on separate continental shelves. Falkion remains a named region without requiring it to be classed as a continent. Their relative positions and a shared campaign-world distance scale have not yet been established.

sections.title: The long wars and the peace
paragraphs: The national histories place the dwarven invasion of Estru and Kyrinus in 80 A.A. New war machines drove the colonies close to defeat. In 200 A.A., Sadion and Everwood combined their armies and began taking the occupied lands back.

Peace was signed in 400 A.A., but the colonies resented the settlement. Estru and Kyrinus rebelled in 500 A.A. Though defeated, they received independence. A century later Estru attacked Sadion and was crushed; Kyrinus declined to join that war.

These dates follow the national histories. Kieran’s account gives a different war duration, and the Akarian history compresses the later separations differently. Those differences remain part of the source review.

sections.title: People and institutions
paragraphs: Cathius Akarian is the recorded emperor of the dwarves. His Battle Ram, Malachi, comes from the mounted tradition he helped establish. His trade with Southern Estru exchanges guns and weapons for rare materials.

Kieran Pelleas leads the Rangers of Larius, a guild of around five hundred elves whose work must meet its own moral standards. His long life reaches back into Everwood’s royal and republican past. The age given in his biography exceeds the lifespan listed for Flatland elves; the reason is not recorded.

Daniel Convor, called Dan or Fox, is a Sadire sergeant of the Legion of Valiance. His record preserves a story of crime, army service and Dole Company. These figures belong to the world’s surviving history; none is designated as the player character.

sections.title: Magic, craft and exploration
paragraphs: Kira’s records place magical craft beside dwarven industry. Kieran’s sheet names elemental spells, healing, resurrection, necromancy, runecrafting, enchanting and alchemy. Cathius’s sheet states that dwarves cannot use magic. The costs, limits and wider availability of these powers have not yet been established.

One surviving thread looks beyond the known lands. A letter bearing the seals of Akaria and Estru offers Kieran and his Rangers a place with a westward exploration fleet. Their account ends as they march for Castle LuCain. The fleet’s destination and what it found remain unrecorded.

records.name: Kira
records.summary: The World of Kira is a homebrew fantasy setting. Its supplied records now cover Larius, TalmahKah, Aldain, Azaloth, Falkion and Bendara, with the most detailed written histories centred on Larius.
records.attribution: World identity and purpose supplied by the user in this conversation; regional identities also occur in the archive directory names.

records.name: Larius
records.summary: The principal recorded region, containing the human, elven and dwarven nations and the Rangers of Larius.
records.scale: Rangers record says continent; no map, coordinates or distances supplied.

records.name: TalmahKah
records.summary: A region represented by a Minecraft reference map with thirty-two named entries and a Word list describing the Lupine.
records.attribution: Regional association comes from the original archive path, not an inferred map.

records.name: Before Ascension / After Ascension
records.summary: The dwarven emergence onto the surface marks the calendar transition. B.A. counts before Ascension; A.A. counts after it. The dwarven history explicitly names 1342 as present day.
records.arithmetic_policy: Year zero is mentioned by the source; no executable civil calendar, month lengths or elapsed-time conversion selected.

records.name: Akarian Empire
records.summary: A dwarven empire centred on Iron Hill and the underground capital Karkaria. Its history describes ten underground cities and five surface cities in 1342 A.A. Cathius Akarian is the recorded emperor.

source_refs.quote: 10 underground cities and 5 above ground cities

records.capability_status: Industrial and military superlatives are source descriptions; exact population, production, stock and force totals are unprovided.

records.name: Kingdom of Sadion
records.summary: The Sadire human kingdom, with Bay Watch as its recorded capital. Its present king is Erik Vollan, whose son is Alek Vollan. Its institutions include the Legion of Valiance, a navy and a Hunter corps.

source_refs.quote: The current king of Sadion is Erik Vollan
the first king to build a Navy and a Hunter corp

records.name: Grand Republic of Evalia
records.summary: The elven republic of Everwood. Its history describes city and village representatives meeting four times a year and gives an assembly total of 256. The current prime minister is unnamed.
records.note: Population subtypes are recorded in the Larius list; their current citizenship and political distribution are not enumerated.

records.name: Kyrinus
records.summary: The Karthinian elven nation, founded as an Evalian colony in 40 A.A. It rebelled in 500 A.A., gained independence after defeat and later renewed trade with Everwood. A non-aggression pact is recorded between the elven nations.

source_refs.quote: they currently have a Non-Aggression pact

records.institution: Karthinian Council mentioned in Kieran’s biography; composition and current officeholders unknown.

records.name: Estru
records.summary: The Estrusian former Sadire colony, independent after the rebellion of 500 A.A. Its invasion of Sadion in 600 A.A. ended in defeat. Kieran’s and Cathius’s records distinguish Southern Estru as an Akarian trading partner.

source_refs.quote: Southern half of the Estrusian Protectorate

records.note: The present constitutional relationship between Estru and its southern part is not established; Castle LuCain’s political location is also unprovided.

records.name: Iron Hill
records.summary: The named heartland above the Akarian underground.

source_refs.quote: underground of what is known today as Iron Hill

records.name: Rangers of Larius
records.summary: Kieran Pelleas’s elven guild takes jobs across Larius that it considers morally acceptable. Its present description gives around 500 elves and names Akaria, Southern Estru and the Evalian republic as clients.

source_refs.quote: The Rangers work for any and all as long as the job is morally acceptable

records.membership: Elves of differing specialties; ancestry and membership do not grant player control.

records.name: Legion of Valiance
records.summary: Founded under Grad Vollan to keep peace in Bay Watch and Sadion. Daniel Convor is recorded as a sergeant.

source_refs.quote: The Legion was made to keep peace of Bay Watch and all of Sadion
Sergeant in the Legion of Valiance

records.name: Dole Company
records.summary: Daniel’s army company. His biography records changes from Captain Dellin to Tiberious and Dougrous Bottlebrewer, with Eagle becoming lieutenant and Daniel sergeant.

source_refs.quote: Dole Company under the command of Captain Dellin
Doug promoted to Captain, Eagle promoted to Lieutenant, and Fox promoted to sergeant

records.note: Doug is not silently equated with Dougrous Bottlebrewer; that reading is retained as an editorial inference pending confirmation.

records.name: Hunter corps
records.summary: A Sadion institution attributed to San Vollan that hunts dangerous criminals across the continent.

source_refs.quote: a Hunter corp (a group of bounty hunters that hunt down the most dangerous criminals on the continent)

records.name: Cathius Akarian
records.summary: The recorded Akarian emperor, age 75, born in 1267. His biography describes a calm, stern and caring ruler who favours underground expansion and trade.

source_refs.quote: Cathius was born in 1267, 75 years before present day
seeks to expand the empire underground rather than above

records.childhood_and_succession: Started public work at 15; styled Revered One at 20; assumed ruling duties after his mother died at 35; crowned after his father died when Cathius was 50.

records.summary: The Akarian history explicitly names 1342 as present day. This is a world reference year, not a selected playthrough date.

records.name: Akarian industry and firearms
records.summary: Akarian sources name Golem’s Flame, refined Golfla gunpowder, Kartac guns and Frikori factories. Cathius’s record describes trade of guns and weapons for rare materials with Southern Estru.

source_refs.quote: called Golfla or in the new tongue Gun Powder
giving them guns and weapons in return for rare materials

records.rule_status: Qualitative source fact; no damage, production, prices, capacities or access privileges adopted.

records.name: Dwarven inability to use magic
records.summary: Cathius’s character record explicitly states that dwarves cannot use magic. This setting-wide statement comes from one character sheet and remains a source rule for review.

source_refs.quote: Spells: None as Dwarves cannot use magic

records.rule_status: Source rule; exceptions, item use and executable enforcement unselected.

records.name: Elven magic and craft
records.summary: The Everwood history describes magical and healing differences among elves. Kieran’s sheet names elemental magic, healing, resurrection, raising the dead, dispelling, runecrafting, enchanting and alchemy.

source_refs.quote: Sea Elves being the most magical

records.rule_status: Named capabilities are retained; costs, limits, access, consequences and IRGS numerical rules are unresolved.

records.name: Westward exploration fleet
records.summary: Kieran’s final recorded scene concerns an exploration fleet heading west, a paid offer sealed by Akaria and Estru, and a march to Castle LuCain. It is a reusable world thread whose destination and outcome are not recorded.

source_refs.quote: The letter told him of the exploration fleet heading west

records.note: TalmahKah is not identified as the fleet’s destination by any supplied document.

continuity_issues.title: Kieran’s longevity
continuity_issues.description: Kieran is 2342 years old; the Flatland Evalian entry gives a lifespan of 1000 years. His Plains identity may correspond to Flatland, but that mapping and any exception remain unconfirmed.
continuity_issues.question: Is Kieran exceptional, is the species lifespan a typical age rather than a limit, or should an old value change?

continuity_issues.title: Duration of the dwarven war
continuity_issues.description: The national histories date the invasion to 80 A.A. and peace to 400 A.A.; Kieran’s biography calls the war 228 years long. The numbers cannot be used as one exact continuous war duration without an explanation.
continuity_issues.question: Does 228 describe Kieran’s participation or one phase, or is a date or duration incorrect?

continuity_issues.title: The rebellion and separation dates
continuity_issues.description: Sadion, Everwood, Kyrinus and Kieran place rebellion and independence around 500 A.A. Akaria’s retrospective describes the peoples splitting in 600 A.A.; it may compress separate developments.
continuity_issues.question: Should 500 A.A. be the political independence date, with 600 A.A. reserved for Estru’s later war?

continuity_issues.title: Estru and Southern Estru
continuity_issues.description: The histories describe Estru’s independence and later defeat, while character sheets refer to Southern Estru and the southern half of an Estrusian Protectorate. No present constitution, border or ruler is specified.
continuity_issues.question: What are Estru’s current political divisions, rulers and relationship with Akaria?

source_refs.quote: Southern half of the Estrusian Protectorate

continuity_issues.title: Map and disputed colonial geography
continuity_issues.description: The user confirms that the six mapped regions sit on separate continental shelves, with Falkion not necessarily considered a continent. Their relative positions, map dates and campaign-world distance scale remain open. Aldain has an explicit political colour key; the written accounts still differ over the last Kyrinus refuge.
continuity_issues.question: What are the relative positions of the six shelves, which dates do the maps represent, and what world-distance scale should apply?

source_refs.quote: one on their land border off the mainland

continuity_issues.title: Spelling and identity variants
continuity_issues.description: The archive uses Arkanian/Akarian/Arkarian, Evalian/Elvanian/Elvalian, Sadion/Sadire and Daniel Conver/Convor. Some are likely spelling variants; others distinguish a people, country or period. Karthi is not silently equated with Karthinian.
continuity_issues.question: Which spellings and people/country distinctions should be canonical?

continuity_issues.title: Magic and technology rules
continuity_issues.description: The sources name firearms and strong magic, including resurrection and raising the dead, without rules for costs, availability, limits or consequences. Dwarven inability to use magic occurs in Cathius’s record.
continuity_issues.question: Which magical capabilities and limitations define Kira, and how widely available are guns and enchanted items?

source_refs.quote: Spells: None as Dwarves cannot use magic

continuity_issues.title: Early Sadion chronology
continuity_issues.description: Sadion’s narrative begins at 2500 B.A. and says “After 2000” before the eight cities and capital, without an explicit unit. Everwood dates Sadire unification and trade to 1998 B.A. These accounts have not been forced into a calculated founding date.
continuity_issues.question: What does “After 2000” mean, and how should Grad and San Vollan fit into the early timeline?

source_refs.quote: The nations opened trade in 1998 B.A

continuity_issues.title: World baseline and authored starting snapshots
continuity_issues.description: 1342 A.A. is explicitly present day, but there is no month, day, time, global census or complete stock/authority snapshot. Character biographies may contain later additions and are not all independently dated.
continuity_issues.question: Which source material belongs to the chosen 1342 world baseline, and which earlier eras should receive separate developed snapshots?

source_refs.quote: Cathius was born in 1267, 75 years before present day

continuity_issues.title: Western expedition and TalmahKah
continuity_issues.description: The exploration fleet is headed west. TalmahKah now has a map with thirty-two entries and five named Lupine communities, but no supplied source explicitly identifies it as the fleet’s destination or records the expedition’s outcome.
continuity_issues.question: Was TalmahKah the intended western destination, and what happened on that expedition?

continuity_issues.title: Map capitals and written place names
continuity_issues.description: The Larius map labels Karwathis at 1 and Evalian at 18, while the histories name Karkaria and Evalia. Ikarion at 24 resembles Ikrarion in Kieran’s account. These could be spelling changes, earlier canon or different places.
continuity_issues.question: Which names should be current canon, and do any of these labels identify different places?

source_refs.quote: moved the capital from Tethris to Evalia

continuity_issues.title: Duplicate number 25 and small map lettering
continuity_issues.description: Larius uses 25 for both Lethar and Sarinus. TalmahKah’s small lettering makes at least Gilsglow worth checking against the original-resolution map. The transcription preserves visible spellings and records uncertainty.
continuity_issues.question: Which map markers belong to Lethar and Sarinus, and are there spelling corrections to the transcribed key?
